capacity_loss_basis.derivation: The loss figure is stated by the source: gross tonnage of ships entering the Gulf of Aden fell >70% between the 1st half of Dec 2023 and the 1st half of Feb 2024; taken as 0.7 (the stated floor). Corroborated in the same timeline by Suez transits -70% by Jun 2024 (UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024). No arithmetic conversion applied. Container-ship capacity fell further (-92% by Jun 2024); 0.7 is the conservative all-shipping figure.

disruption_notes: capacity_loss 0.7 = observed gross-tonnage fall through the Gulf of Aden (>70% by mid-Feb 2024, UNCTAD); container-ship capacity fell further (-92% by Jun 2024). expected_duration_d 559 = days from 2023-11-19 to the last timeline observation (2025-05-31, Suez tonnage still ~70% below 2023) - an observed lower bound, not a forecast; the disruption had not resolved in the source timeline.

observed_steps.effect: Incident involving the car carrier Galaxy Leader in the Red Sea - first of a series of incidents that led carriers to avoid the corridor (crew held until 22 Jan 2025).
observed_steps.evidence_source: AI Timeline compilation of the crisis chronology: https://aitimeline.in/red-sea-shipping-attacks-rerouting-costs-timeline-14731/

observed_steps.effect: Onset of sustained carrier diversions away from the Red Sea corridor (UNCTAD reference timeline).
By end of December 2023, traffic through the Suez Canal was down by about half vs pre-crisis levels.
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024, via Maritime Executive: https://maritime-executive.com/article/unctad-maritime-chokepoints-are-trade-s-biggest-vulnerability

observed_steps.effect: Spot container rates roughly doubled on Shanghai-Rotterdam between 1 Dec 2023 and 1 Feb 2024 (window end date). observed_delay_d is the MODELED one-way transit added by the Cape reroute (census: bypass +~3,000-6,000 nm), not a figure stated by the source.
Gross tonnage of ships entering the Gulf of Aden fell >70% (1st half Dec 2023 to 1st half Feb 2024 window).

Cape of Good Hope arrivals up +85% gross tonnage (7-day moving average, first week of Mar 2024) vs first half of Dec 2023; containership arrivals at the Cape up +328%. observed_delay_d is the MODELED one-way transit added by the Cape reroute, not a figure stated by the source.
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD based on Clarksons Research, via Africa Ports: https://africaports.co.za/2024/04/24/feature-red-sea-crisis-and-implications-for-trade-facilitation-in-africa/

observed_steps.effect: Suez transits -70% vs mid-Dec 2023 (by Jun 2024). Canal revenue fell $9.4B (FY2022/23) to $7.2B (FY2023/24); transits 25,911 to 20,148.
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024, via AI Timeline summary: https://aitimeline.in/red-sea-shipping-attacks-rerouting-costs-timeline-14731/

observed_steps.effect: Cape of Good Hope arrivals +89% (by Jun 2024). Median Asia-Europe round trip cost approx $1.0M via Suez vs $1.7M via the Cape. observed_delay_d is the MODELED one-way transit added by the Cape reroute, not a figure stated by the source.
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024, via AI Timeline summary: https://aitimeline.in/red-sea-shipping-attacks-rerouting-costs-timeline-14731/

observed_steps.effect: Container-ship capacity entering the Gulf of Aden -92% (by Jun 2024). Rerouting raised overall vessel demand by ~3% and container-ship demand by ~12% (UNCTAD via Splash247).
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024, via AI Timeline summary: https://aitimeline.in/red-sea-shipping-attacks-rerouting-costs-timeline-14731/

observed_steps.effect: Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) averaged 2,496 points in 2024, +149% year on year (rate channel; node is the index's home port).
observed_steps.evidence_source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2025, via Lift Europe: https://lift-europe.com/blog-detail/un-global-shipping-faces-weak-growth-2025-rerouting-costs-and-new-rules-reshape-trade

observed_steps.effect: Suez tonnage still approximately 70% below its 2023 level - no full recovery 17 months in.
